summary: Adversarial verification of wf/design/architecture.md. The overall shape holds up: one Next.js application, typed ports, invalidation by changed record type, identity through XS-01/XS-05/XS-03 with no DEMO banner or switcher, and a correct Slice-1 classification (9/24/38, matching repo-baseline.json). All 27 flows.json steps are covered across the 39 rows. The Release defect (D4/HD-1), the device chain with no IA approval and no Decline, publish/release granting no access, and feedback only after Completed are all correct against the boards. Refuted or incomplete: (1) the TE-3 WEB stand-in gives the signed-in Student, via Launch WEB, the only sample-mode path to SIMULATION_COMPLETED, and stamps those events with a production source id (critical, BC3). (2) Completion is typed as derived from runtime activity and marked CONFIRMED, although BC3 says never derive one state from another (major). (3) Browser persistence is presented as fitting the constraints, but B8-06 says 'persistence stay[s] out until decided', and FUNCTIONAL_PARITY_MATRIX §G excludes the localStorage schema-version chain. No exception is recorded for it (major). (4) The spine-start seed contradicts Flow A/B: Godavari, ACC-0107, Rahul and Arun cannot exist before REQ-0042 is approved, and a pre-seeded SACC-0311 breaks B2-13 f0–f3 (major). (5) The boundary plan misses that @xr/contracts exports only '.', so @xr/contracts/draft/* imports fail xr/resolved-boundaries (notExported). It also puts World types in @xr/sample-platform while @xr/domain's decide(command, world) needs them, which is a forbidden domain→sample-platform import (major). (6) The test-hook and stand-in scope versus ARCH §14 is ambiguous, and the WEB stand-in page has no route or allowed home (major). (7) Seven stakeholder↔v46 conflicts that touch these flows are marked CONFIRMED instead of being flagged; only STK31-28 is flagged (major). There are also 15 minor errors: nav count, id counters, provisional BRs labelled CONFIRMED, the omitted ST-15, the Vendor 'Submitted' label, the 'default' release wording, the PU-10 bearer URL, the SSO default, a missing RES record, and Next.js client-only details.

checksRun.check: (a) flows.json coverage: 27 steps (A4 B4 C3 D4 E5 F4 Device3) mapped to the 39 rows of §4.2–§4.8
checksRun.detail: Every flows.json step maps to a row: E2 is split into E2a/E2b, F3 into F3a–c and C2 into C2a–d. The row count of 39 and the 10 rows in §4.9 are correct.

checksRun.check: (a) actors and screens per step against flows.json and the boards
checksRun.detail: Actors are correct, and D4 is correctly re-attributed to the System (B4-06 f7–f9 and B4-14 f6 controls have no Release). Screen deviations: C3 drops ST-15, although flows.json lists 'ST-10 / ST-15' and B3-05 f0 has a 'Give feedback on WEB' control. A2 says 'SA nav count 3 → 4', but B1-10 f0 and B7-00 say 3 under review = REQ-0042, REQ-0040, REQ-0038, so the count goes 2 → 3. A3 says 'Internal route: ACC-0107 activated', but ACC-0107 belongs to external REQ-0042 and is created after payment (B1-08 f8); the internal sample is REQ-0039 (B1-08 f9).

checksRun.check: (a) forbidden side effects: publish or release granting access, launch completing, feedback before Completed, IA approving a device transfer, Decline
checksRun.detail: The flow tables are clean: E4 and F3a change no INST/ACC/SACC/FCM, Dv2 is forward-only, Dv3 is approve-only, A3 has no Decline, and C3 is gated on Completed. However, the TE-3 sample-mode mechanism makes the Student's 'Launch WEB' the only path that reaches SIMULATION_COMPLETED for WEB (see the critical correction).

checksRun.check: (a) status labels: CONFIRMED vs the business-rule status in decisions-rules.json
checksRun.detail: Rows marked CONFIRMED rest on PROVISIONAL rules: BR-078 (D1 Ready and 'no make-available control'; B4-11 f15 says 'The make-available step itself is open (T-18)'), BR-111 (F-alt), BR-087 (D2) and BR-099 (§6.2). Dv1 states 'One open request at a time' as a rule, but OD-B3-03 is open.

The proposed row ['@xr/contracts','@xr/domain','@xr/validation'], the addition to @xr/web and the FORBIDDEN_THIRD_PARTY entry are the right matrix edits. Missed: the WorkspacePackage union in boundaries.d.mts; tsconfig.build.json with composite, noEmitOnError and references; tsconfig.solution.json; and the package's own eslint.config with boundaries('@xr/sample-platform'). The boundaries test auto-discovers packages, so it does not need to 'list' the new one.

At 1b090c9, @xr/contracts package.json exports only '.'. resolved-boundaries.mjs rejects any bare workspace subpath that is not in the exports map ('notExported'). The planned imports of '@xr/contracts/draft/ports/*' from apps/web and @xr/sample-platform are therefore rejected.

checksRun.check: (b) domain purity vs the decide(command, world, …) signature
checksRun.detail: §1.2 puts 'World types' in @xr/sample-platform, while @xr/domain's decide and apply take the world. Domain's allowed dependency list is [], so it cannot import the World type.

checksRun.check: (c) no DEMO banner and no account selector in product UI
checksRun.detail: §2.3 keeps sample accounts out of the UI, which matches BR-006 and B8-03 ('Sign in looks like a product … no account switcher'). XS-05 matches board 05 (name · workspace · institution · My device · Help · separator · Sign out).

checksRun.check: (c) honest handling of ARCHITECTURE §14 and FUNCTIONAL_PARITY_MATRIX §G
checksRun.detail: TE-1…TE-5 are recorded. Not recorded: browser persistence (FPM §G 'localStorage namespace and schema-version chain'); the test-hook build flag and data-source switch (env/index.ts 'there are no prototype flags'); client rendering of public pages (ARCH §4 'Public discovery … server-rendered'); and the test hooks in 'sample builds' (reset world, advance clock, set payment outcome, emit runtime events), which are stand-in controls and a demo clock (ARCH §14).

checksRun.check: (d) persistence vs 'no backend persistence' and 'apps/web is not the business backend'
checksRun.detail: Option C (a server world in Next route handlers) is rightly rejected. Option B is browser-only, so it does not make apps/web a backend. But B8-06 'Mock services' reads 'Real auth, payment, XR runtimes, grading automation and persistence stay out until decided', which is broader than the BC10/README 'backend persistence'. The document cites only the narrower wording.

checksRun.check: (e) five-state read models: is any state derived from another?
checksRun.detail: ⑤ completion is typed as 'derived from ④ by a replaceable policy' and marked CONFIRMED, but BC3 says 'Never derive one from another'. Invariant 2 ('No command at all writes ⑤') contradicts BC3's 'Completed is set by the system'. experimentGate, formatAvailability, canOpenFormat, usage and feedbackEntry combine states into gates without rewriting them, which is acceptable.

The approach is consistent overall: §6.1 makes every sample-mode page client-rendered because the world and session live only in browser storage (AD-12). Not stated: SessionGate and WorkspaceGuard must be client components ('use client'), since layout.tsx defaults to a server component that cannot read sessionStorage or localStorage. Also missing: the pre-hydration render, Suspense around useSearchParams for the '?step=' wizards, and client-set document titles. The WEB stand-in 'simulation tab' needs a Next route, which is absent from the §6.1 tree and cannot live in a package that forbids framework-web.

This matches board 08 'In context': 'The refusal does not replace the shell … nothing in it is marked current'. Choosing the shell by session role in the parent layout and guarding in the child layout is feasible.

The counts are 9 SAFE, 24 SALVAGE_WITH_CHANGES and 38 DISCARD, and each file's class matches. No rejected UI is reused: every packages/ui/src/*.tsx file, app/(connected)/**, demo-bar, demo-accounts-screen*, features/** and the e2e spec are DISCARD. The quotes check out against the working tree ('The caller is never a parameter' in services/access/types.ts:7; 'refusals write nothing' in access-adapter.test.ts:104). Minor: §9 says 'Each file was re-read', but §12 lists only six Slice-1 files as checked.

checksRun.check: Spine-start seed and id counters vs board references
checksRun.detail: Godavari is created by approving REQ-0042 (B1-13; B2-00 'new institution created by approving REQ-0042'). The 12 students, including Rahul, Priya and Arun, were imported on 8 Oct, after that approval. B2-04: SACC-0311 and SACC-0312 are 'later sample states (12 Oct)'. B2-13 f0: on 9 Oct 'his group has no grant yet'. Boards also show ids above the flow ids: REQ-0058 (IA-17, 21 Oct), SUB-0079…0086, UPD-0006/0007, DTR-0019 and ATT-0451.

checksRun.check: Stakeholder↔v46 conflicts surfaced for the owner
checksRun.detail: Only STK31-28 is flagged (AD-30). Flow rows marked CONFIRMED silently follow v46 where decisions-rules.json#conflicts records a stakeholder conflict: 07.3 R16 (CM direct link edit, F1), 07.2-F/07.3 R17 (SA override scope, E-alt3), 07.2-E (SA edits the platform code, §4.9), PM-09 (sequential gating, Flow C), PM-08 (timer, D2), STK31-26 (CSV columns, B3 importStudents) and STK31-21/24 (SA creates tenants, Flow A).

corrections.location: wf/design/architecture.md §2.6 TE-3; §4.4 C2a–C2c; §1.2 mock adapter row (stand-ins)
corrections.problem: In sample builds, TE-3 makes the WEB stand-in 'simulation' tab, opened from the Student's own 'Launch WEB' (C2a), the only source of SIMULATION_COMPLETED for WEB. The page acts for the signed-in Student. Either it emits completion automatically (completion inferred from a launch or from time) or through a control the Student presses (completion set by the Student). Both are forbidden by BC3. Moving the control to another tab does not avoid FPM §G's exclusion of a 'stand-in completion control on the Student's run screen'. The stand-in also stamps events with the production source 'web-runtime', so stand-in completions are indistinguishable from real runtime data, which defeats the deliberate exclusion of stand-in sources. The 'labelled stand-in page' also puts developer/demo wording into a product path.
corrections.evidence: START-HERE BC3: 'Completed is set by the system, never by the Student, and never inferred from a launch'. B3-03 f3 caption: 'Completion comes only from the simulation (T-12). No “I have finished” button.' 1b090c9:v2/packages/domain/src/runtime/events.ts RUNTIME_SOURCES comment: stand-in sources 'are excluded from V2 (docs/FUNCTIONAL_PARITY_MATRIX.md §G)'. 1b090c9:v2/docs/FUNCTIONAL_PARITY_MATRIX.md §G row: 'In-page stand-in completion control on the Student's run screen … V2 implements the contract, not the stand-in'. B8-03 'Developer / demo wording 0'.
corrections.correction: Rewrite TE-3 and C2b/C2c as follows. (1) The WEB stand-in reached from 'Launch WEB' may emit only SIMULATION_LAUNCHED, SESSION_STARTED and SESSION_ENDED; it must have no completion control and no timer-based completion. (2) SIMULATION_COMPLETED, for WEB as well as headset formats, is emitted only through the test-hook or fixture path from §2.5, never from a page the signed-in Student operates. If the owner wants reviewers to see 'Completed' in a hosted sample build, record that explicitly as an owner-authorised exception naming who triggers it. (3) Keep the domain enum and the wire schema unchanged, but record a sample-only provenance on every stand-in event inside the @xr/sample-platform envelope (e.g. origin: 'sample-standin'), so stand-in events stay distinguishable. (4) Remove 'labelled' wording from any page reachable from product navigation. (5) Mark C2c's mechanism UNRESOLVED (T-12) instead of 'PROVISIONAL (stand-in)'.

corrections.location: wf/design/architecture.md §5.1 type ⑤; §5.2 row ⑤; §5.5 invariant 2; §1.3 completion/ module; §4.4 C2c
corrections.problem: Learning completion (⑤) is defined as 'written by NOBODY; derived from ④ by a replaceable policy' over the runtime event log, and is marked CONFIRMED. BC3 forbids deriving any of the five states from another, and says Completed is 'set by the system', which is a write. Invariant 2 ('No command at all writes ⑤') states the opposite of the owner wording. The tension with committed ARCH §8 ('progress (per technology) … Derived, never stored as truth') and with utilisation.ts, which hard-codes SIMULATION_COMPLETED as the trigger, is not flagged.
corrections.evidence: START-HERE BC3 ('five different states. Never derive one from another … “Completed” is set by the system'). decisions-rules.json BR-024 (CONFIRMED-STAKEHOLDER). 1b090c9:v2/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8 'Derived, never stored as truth … progress (per technology)'. 1b090c9:v2/packages/domain/src/runtime/utilisation.ts header ('COMPLETED needs a completion event'). The task brief lists utilisation.ts hard-coding SIMULATION_COMPLETED as an open T-12 conflict.
corrections.correction: (1) Model ⑤ as its own system-written record, e.g. CompletionRecord {personId, experimentId, format, completedAt, triggerRef}. A system completion handler (not a user command) writes it when the completion event decided by T-12 is accepted. formatProgress then reads ④ and ⑤ side by side. (2) Change invariant 2 to 'Only the system completion handler writes ⑤; no user-facing command, launch, resource, assessment or other format does'. (3) Downgrade §5.2 row ⑤ and C2c to CONFIRMED (who may not set it) · PROVISIONAL (mechanism) · UNRESOLVED (T-12 trigger). (4) Add an owner decision: BC3 versus ARCH §8 / utilisation.ts on whether completion is a derived read model or a stored system fact.

corrections.location: wf/design/architecture.md §6.1 '(public) requests/[ticket]'; §6.4 PU-10; AD-13
corrections.problem: An opaque ticket in the URL path works as a bearer link: anyone who has the URL opens the request status. The boards draw no lookup, link or magic link, and the design keeps the status 'from this session'. The text does not say whether the URL ticket alone is enough or whether it must match the sessionStorage ticket.
corrections.evidence: B1-08: 'The reference number identifies the request — it does not open the page on its own. No reference lookup, OTP, magic link or account registration is designed.' B1-07: 'Check request status, continues from this session … the page promises no link, e-mail or account.'
corrections.correction: Use a capability-free route such as /requests/status (and /requests/status/payment) that resolves the ticket held in this browser session. Alternatively, state that /requests/[ticket] renders only when the path ticket equals a ticket held in this session (or the viewer is the signed-in IA of that institution), and otherwise renders the public not-found pattern. Record this under AD-13.

corrections.problem: The recommended sample-mode default is to render B1-09 f6 ('Institution sign-in unavailable') at all times. That hides the stakeholder-confirmed 'Sign in with your institution' entry that the drawn default f0 shows.
corrections.evidence: BR-008 (CONFIRMED-STAKEHOLDER): 'Sign in offers “Sign in with your institution (SSO)” and “Sign in with e-mail”'. B8-03: 'Institution sign-in + e-mail sign-in; no account switcher (B1-09)'. B1-09 f0 controls include 'Sign in with your institution'.
corrections.correction: Recommend the drawn sequence f0 → (click) f5 'Institution sign-in starting' → f6 'unavailable'. Offer the permanent f6 only as the alternative for the owner to choose.

corrections.location: wf/design/architecture.md §3.2 'What lives where' (SEL, PU-10 ticket, drafts in sessionStorage); §2.3 per-tab session
corrections.problem: sessionStorage is per tab, but B1-06 says the selection lives in the visitor's browser session. A selection or ticket held in one tab disappears in a tab opened from the catalogue. The per-tab session is also missing in the new tabs the product itself opens (ST-06 resources, ST-08 'opened in a new tab'), and every deep link opened in a new tab forces a new sign-in. None of these consequences is stated.
corrections.evidence: B1-06: 'The selection lives in the visitor’s browser session until the request is sent'. B3-03 f0: 'opened in a new tab'. B3-01 'Opened in a new tab just now' (surface-student.json fieldEvidence).
corrections.correction: State the per-tab consequence and either accept it explicitly (AD-07) or keep SEL and the ticket in localStorage under a browser-session marker. Say how the WEB stand-in tab learns the person, e.g. from a nonce handed over by launchFormat, without putting personal data in the URL.

corrections.evidence: 1b090c9:v2/apps/web/src/app/providers.tsx ('use client' pattern); 1b090c9:v2/apps/web/package.json next 16.3.4; deliverable §12 'Next.js 16 behaviour … assumed … not tested'.
corrections.correction: Add: 'The (workspace) and (public) layouts stay server components that render client <SessionGate>, <WorkspaceShell> and <WorkspaceGuard>. Storage is read through useSyncExternalStore with a null server snapshot. Before hydration the drawn Loading state renders. Wizard pages wrap their useSearchParams consumer in <Suspense>. Titles are set on the client from the view model.'
